column1: Vale/s0|Does the hat stay on in wind?|Not without care. Keeping rain off spectacles does not make it immune to weather.|Did your sister make it for you alone?|Yes. She considered the size a solution rather than an apology.

Vale/s1|Would you prefer I didn't ask?|A polite question is welcome. Assuming an audience is owed a performance is what tires me.|Why keep such a noticeable hat?|It does the job my sister intended, whatever strangers make of it.
Vale/e0|Has it caught on a door before?|Once was quite instructive.|Would a smaller hat be easier?|For doorways, certainly. My spectacles retain a vote on rainy days.
Vale/e1|Was breakfast really that ordinary?|Entirely. I consider that its finest quality.|Would you rather enjoy the quiet?|For a little while, yes. Thank you for asking.

Vale/w0|What quiet work interests you?|Reading and thinking without having to demonstrate loyalty in every conclusion.|Has he accused you personally?|I am describing the suspicion encouraged by his rule, not claiming a private audience.|Why would harmless oddness trouble him?|It is difficult to control what one refuses to understand.

Vale/w1|Do you expect people to become less suspicious?|Gradually, if they learn that unfamiliar does not mean dangerous.|Will you keep the large hat?|My sister would be delighted by the suggestion that politics might finally shrink it.|What would you like to do first?|Finish an ordinary piece of work without anyone making it an allegory for the state.

Cerys/s0|What kind of notes do you compare?|What a record says beside what people describe experiencing.|Could the spoken stories be wrong too?|Certainly. Comparing sources is not choosing whichever one sounds warmer.
Cerys/s1|Why learn through losing?|A loss can reveal a mistake, if I understand the rules first.|Do you keep the stakes small?|Very. Tuition need not consume supper.
Cerys/e0|Do you and your sister agree?|Not always. That is one reason comparing notes is useful.|Do the questions spoil supper?|Only when we forget to eat while discussing them.

Cerys/e1|Can a good decision still lose a hand?|Yes. Understanding a game includes accepting chance.|Do you ask the others to explain?|After the hand, when they cannot benefit from misleading me about the immediate choice.

Cerys/w0|Why trust a whispered account?|I do not trust it merely because it is whispered. Fear tells me something about the setting, not whether every detail is true.|Do the written facts agree with it?|Sometimes, sometimes not. That is where the checking begins.|Do you record private stories?|With care and permission. A source's safety matters more than an interesting note.

Cerys/w1|Which awkward parts must remain?|Mistakes, disagreements and harm that a tidy victory account might skip.|What if the records and witnesses conflict?|Keep both visible and investigate, rather than hiding whichever is inconvenient.|Will you and your sister keep comparing notes?|Yes. Being relieved gives us no reason to stop checking.

Nyra/s0|What should I watch when Dain deals?|Both hands and the cards, while ensuring everyone has agreed on the rules.|Did your uncle cheat people?|He performed tricks for an audience. That is a different agreement from a wager.

Nyra/s1|Does explaining the trick spoil it?|Not necessarily. But an audience agrees to a performance, not to being robbed.|Do you enjoy being fooled yourself?|When the surprise is the entertainment and I chose to take part.

Nyra/e0|How can you tell they're enjoying it?|Reactions offer clues. A good performer also accepts when an audience is not interested.|What if someone wants to leave?|Then the performance should let them. It is not a trap.

Nyra/e1|Has Dain dealt unevenly before?|Enough suspicious deals have justified careful counting.|Could you enjoy an honest game with him?|Yes. Watching him obey his own rules could be an additional entertainment.

Nyra/w0|What deception do you mean?|The story that every demand benefits the people paying it, regardless of what they experience.|Does everyone believe it?|No. Being required to applaud can conceal disagreement.|How can people challenge it?|Compare promises with results and allow the people affected to speak plainly.

Nyra/w1|What words would you examine first?|Promises with no clear terms, costs or person answerable for keeping them.|Could a charming leader still be useful?|Of course. Charm simply cannot substitute for the work.|When should we applaud?|After understanding what was done and whom it helped, rather than just the performance around it.

Maren/s0|Were you worried about the wet floor?|I dried it. Welcoming a soaked guest was the immediate job.|Did his family become regular guests?|They returned when their travels brought them this way.

Maren/s1|Can tired guests always get that room?|When it is available. I cannot promise every visitor the same bed.|What if someone needs an easier entrance?|I discuss what accommodation we actually have rather than promise a room that will not suit them.

Maren/e0|Do you charge for the towels?|Ordinary drying is part of welcoming a guest, not a surprise penalty for rain.|What if several guests arrive wet?|More towels, then dealing with the floor so nobody slips.

Maren/e1|Why pay attention to the foot of the bed?|An uncomfortable fold is easy to miss while making it and easy to feel while trying to sleep.|Do you check every room?|Yes. Familiar work still deserves a proper check.

Maren/w0|Do you keep a list for soldiers?|I keep the records the inn needs. I dislike guests feeling that a bed is another checkpoint.|Why are guests so worried?|People have been questioned on the roads and expect the same indoors.|Can you promise nobody will disturb them?|I can do my best and be honest. I cannot control every officer's demand.

Maren/w1|Why did guests used to leave so early?|Some hoped to avoid patrols or questions. Others simply had a long journey.|Did the family seem more relaxed?|They made plans for a second day instead of treating the room as a brief hiding place.|Will the inn become busier?|I hope so. I would welcome complaints about ordinary full bookings.

Dunstan/s0|What had you done wrong?|I had not made the hilt sound enough for the strain it would take.|Why display a failed blade?|A clear example makes a lesson harder to turn into vague pride or shame.

Dunstan/s1|How do you check a good fit?|Movement and an honest report from the wearer, as well as inspection.|Can fitting wait until battle?|That is a terrible time to discover a restricted shoulder. Deal with it beforehand.

Dunstan/e0|What if the wearer is embarrassed to complain?|I remind them this is fitting, not gratitude. I need an accurate answer.|Could the armor fit one person and pinch another?|Easily. Similar size does not mean identical movement.

Dunstan/e1|Do you still have the first blade?|Kept as a teaching piece, not equipment anyone should trust in battle.|Do you tell apprentices how it failed?|Yes. Hiding the reason would turn a useful example into an ornament.

Dunstan/h|What do smiths need beyond ore?|Fuel, tools, water, food and trained people. None arrives by admiring a furnace.|Did you learn from neighbouring craftspeople?|Certainly. A workshop becomes poorer when pride prevents a useful question.

Dunstan/w0|Would you refuse to make a weapon?|I consider the work and its purpose. A royal demand does not make that consideration unnecessary.|What protection can your craft offer?|Sound equipment fitted properly, and honest advice about its limits.|Do you prefer making tools?|I enjoy work whose everyday usefulness I can see without counting injuries.

Dunstan/w1|What will you teach new smiths first?|Care around the work, sound methods, and admitting a fault before passing it on.|Will weapons still be needed?|The roads still have dangers. I hope fewer orders serve a ruler's appetite for conflict.|What makes a tool successful?|Doing its job reliably and being maintained, not simply looking fine when it leaves the shop.

Sela/s0|Can a flaw ever make glass unsafe?|Certainly. Enjoying its appearance does not remove the need to judge its strength and use.|Do you disclose flaws when selling?|Yes. The buyer should know what the piece is suited for.

Sela/s1|Did you test the glass again?|Many times, with different samples. One survival was a clue, not a guarantee.|Why did the frame fail first?|The materials responded differently. Understanding the whole construction mattered as much as admiring the glass.

Sela/e0|Do spectators distract you?|Sometimes. I ask them to stand where they can watch without interrupting the work.|Does the shape change quickly?|At certain stages. The person working needs attention more than an audience's suspense.

Sela/e1|When would you reject a bubble?|When it compromises the purpose or soundness of the piece.|Can an ornament use glass a window cannot?|Sometimes. The demands differ, but I still inspect the material.

Sela/h|Which tools do the trades share?|Furnace fittings and shaped metal tools, among others.|Does Dunstan understand glasswork?|Enough to make useful tools with clear instructions. Each craft still has its own expertise.

Sela/w0|Did danger inspire the shield?|It made reliable protection feel worth the work and failed experiments.|Would you stop making protection if peace improved?|There would still be dangerous work and journeys. I would welcome less urgent demand.|Can one invention solve that danger?|No. Good equipment helps; it cannot repair the decisions causing every injury.

Sela/w1|What would you like to make?|Something shaped for light and pleasure, with no battle expected of it.|Would you still help travellers?|Of course. Wanting a different project does not erase the people needing existing work.|Is beautiful work easier?|Not necessarily. It would simply present a difficulty I could enjoy for another reason.

Tam/s0|Why had the screw been left unused?|The press had become too troublesome to operate. An apron was less demanding.|Did Joss really improve it?|It turns smoothly now. His claim about when it was new is harder to check.
Tam/s1|Does Nan accept the cider?|With explanations about why it was unnecessary, followed by accepting it.|Why not just call it a gift?|We do, eventually. The argument has become part of the visit.

Tam/e0|Does it still catch at that point?|No. Joss remembers where it used to, and checks out of habit.|Was repairing it worth the work?|It returned a useful tool to use instead of leaving it as a hook.

Tam/e1|What would Nan like to take home?|Something useful she would choose herself. A gift should not merely clear my shelves.|Does she do the same to you?|Constantly. Neither of us is winning, which suits us.

Tam/w0|Can you estimate the harvest early?|Only within limits. Fruit does not follow the collector's preferred forecast.|What happens after a poor season?|We have less to share and the same pressure to meet the demand.|Does Joss help with the apples?|Yes. The work and the worry have been shared.

Tam/w1|Will you make more cider?|If the fruit and our needs allow. We can decide after seeing the actual crop.|Will Nan come for supper?|I hope so. Planning a visit is a much nicer use of a good harvest.|What changes most for you?|Knowing the first claim on the fruit can be the household and neighbours who grew it.

Celia/s0|Why was a laundry list with the battle account?|It had been tucked among the pages. I recorded that without pretending to know the writer's reason.|Could an ordinary list be historically useful?|Yes, if its date and context can be established. Ordinary does not mean uninformative.

Celia/s1|How would you answer that question?|Look for letters and local accounts written at the time, not just later speeches.|Why reserve the last page?|It reminds me that a finished notebook need not mean a finished subject.

Celia/e0|Could you write another question there?|Of course. The empty space is a reminder, not a sacred rule.|What happens when the notebook fills?|I begin another rather than forcing the world to stop providing questions.

Celia/e1|Do you know who wrote the list?|Not certainly. I keep that uncertainty attached to the copy.|Why copy the ordinary wording exactly?|Small details can become evidence later. Tidying them to sound important would lose that.

Celia/h|Do rulers' dates still matter?|Yes. They help place events, but cannot describe every life between them.|What can letters add?|How people understood events while living through them, with all the limits of that perspective.

Celia/w0|How do you know people disagreed?|Accounts and conversations that contradict the official claim of unanimous belief.|Could your notebook miss quieter supporters?|Yes. I must not replace one claim about everyone with another.|Why record disagreement?|It shows that people had choices and thoughts the official summary erased.

Celia/w1|Will you include opinions you dislike?|If relevant, represented accurately rather than made easy to dismiss.|How do you record a conversation fairly?|With permission where needed, clear wording, and a chance to correct misunderstandings.|Does disagreement weaken the new beginning?|Not necessarily. Being able to discuss it openly can make decisions better.

Ivo/s0|Where do you keep the inherited tools?|At home, secured on a rack where I can see and care for them.|Do you use them too?|The sound ones suited to the job. Age and affection are not substitutes for inspection.

Ivo/s1|Why is the lid difficult?|Small errors in the box's shape become obvious when two edges must meet.|Have you asked for help?|Yes. I would rather learn why it catches than force it shut indefinitely.

Ivo/e0|What makes that corner catch?|I need to check the fit and alignment. Pressing harder is a symptom, not a repair.|Will you call it finished soon?|When it closes properly and remains sound, not merely when I tire of it.

Ivo/e1|Can cleaning reveal damage?|Yes. Handling a tool carefully makes wear easier to notice.|Did your grandfather teach you that?|He did. Preparing a tool is part of the work, not an optional ceremony afterwards.

Ivo/w0|What useful things did your grandfather make?|Boxes, fittings, repairs that helped ordinary work continue.|Do all royal orders concern weapons?|No. I am troubled by how much attention destructive work receives.|What would you rather build?|Things someone can use for years without needing an enemy.

Ivo/w1|What would improve the tool chest?|Places that hold the tools securely and make them easy to inspect and reach.|Will you finish the small box first?|Yes. It is teaching me faults I should not enlarge into a chest.|Who would use the chest?|Someone doing the work it is arranged for. I ought to ask before deciding every compartment.

Merrin/s0|Does your brother send word now?|When he can. Some habits survive more reasonable arrangements.|Why not sit somewhere more comfortable?|I choose a place that suits both waiting and sitting. A view is not worth an aching back all day.

Merrin/s1|Do people really worry about interrupting?|Often. A ready place can make the welcome easier to believe.|What if you need an evening alone?|Then I say so kindly. Welcoming visitors should not require abandoning every need of my own.

Merrin/e0|Why move the cup from the edge?|To avoid knocking it over while making room. Hospitality need not begin with cleaning a spill.|Do you always expect your brother?|Not always. There are other people I enjoy seeing too.

Merrin/e1|Do you ever mistake a stranger for him?|At a sound, briefly. Looking up settles it.|Does waiting trouble you?|More when the roads are uncertain. Ordinary late arrival is easier to forgive than unexplained danger.

Merrin/w0|Do the patrols delay your family?|Sometimes. They add uncertainty to visits that should be simple.|Have you asked them about a traveller?|I prefer reliable news from someone who actually saw the person.|What would useful watching mean?|Noticing someone who needs help, rather than inventing a reason to detain them.

Merrin/w1|Who are you hoping to see first?|My brother, if the route and his work allow it.|Would you visit him instead?|Possibly. It would be pleasant to make the planning about company rather than fear.|Will you still keep the spare place?|Yes. That habit was never the king's to take away.

Zella/s0|Do small holes grow under strain?|They can, which makes an early sound repair worthwhile.|Should the largest tear wait?|Not if the net is needed. Mother's lesson was about neglect, not ignoring an urgent failure.

Zella/s1|How did cord rescue the toy?|We could reach and catch it without a child leaning dangerously into the drain.|Do you replace the cord after using it?|If it is damaged or no longer long enough for useful work.

Zella/e0|What if the mesh around it is worn?|Then the repair must include sound material, not just close the visible gap.|Do you inspect the whole net?|Yes. One small hole may not be the only trouble.

Zella/e1|Do you measure before cutting?|Enough for the job and the knots, rather than the bare distance alone.|Have you cut a piece too short?|Yes. It is an efficient way to learn how little wishing lengthens cord.

Zella/w0|What makes a knot different from his promise?|Someone can inspect and test my work. He dislikes people testing his claims.|Have royal promises failed here?|Often enough that people compare them with actual conditions rather than the proclamation.|Can words ever be dependable?|Yes, when the person making them accepts responsibility for keeping them.

Zella/w1|How can people test a public promise?|Ask what will be done, by when, with what means, and who will answer if it fails.|What if circumstances change?|Explain the change honestly instead of pretending the original promise meant something else.|Can a promise be repaired?|Trust can sometimes be rebuilt through clear corrections and work actually done.

Iris/s0|Were you able to leave another way?|There was a way out. My mistake was keeping too little dry fuel accessible for the night.|Did you change the wood storage afterwards?|Yes. I make sure enough is indoors before severe weather, without blocking exits or crowding the hearth.

Iris/s1|Did you tell her she could simply visit?|Yes. She still enjoyed arriving with a reason, so I stopped arguing with the kindling.|Were you glad of the company too?|Very. It was not only her evening being improved.

Iris/e0|How much do you bring in?|Enough for the expected weather, stored sensibly with clear access through the room.|Do you check the doors too?|Yes. Preparing one useful thing should not make another harder to reach.
Iris/e1|What if the errand is genuine?|Then they get help with it as well as a welcome.|Do you visit them too?|Of course. Company should not depend on one person always knocking.

Iris/w0|Why collect after winter stores are stacked?|They can see what is there and call it available, ignoring why it was saved.|Can you explain the household's needs?|I can. They have not always been willing to count them as seriously as the crown's.|What happens when too much is taken?|People face the cold with fewer choices, some of them poor ones.

Iris/w1|Will you store extra wood now?|When possible, while leaving enough forest to recover and space to store it safely.|Do neighbours still need help?|Yes. Ending a levy does not replace what was already lost.|What will you check before next winter?|Fuel, doors and the ordinary preparations I once thought could wait.

Alderic/s0|Did ordinary work help you keep watch?|It gave the waiting useful tasks. Neglect would not have made me more ready.|Were you ever tempted to leave?|I have questioned the long wait. Keeping a duty does not mean never feeling its weight.

Alderic/s1|Do any accounts describe her kindness?|Some impressions survive, though not enough for a complete life.|Could a powerful dragon also be gentle?|Strength and gentleness are not opposites. What matters is how the strength is used.

Alderic/e0|Does the sweeping ever feel pointless?|Repetition can, but a cared-for threshold still serves the next arrival.|What else does keeping watch require?|Maintaining what can be maintained and preserving the knowledge entrusted here.

Alderic/e1|Do all rider images show battle?|No. Accounts and carvings can preserve other gestures and duties too.|How should I interpret an old carving?|Carefully, with context. A damaged gesture does not justify a whole invented story.

Alderic/h|Why leave knowledge in temples?|So it could outlast its original keepers and be found by later riders.|Does finding a Heartstone teach everything?|No. Power and understanding need to grow together through careful use.

Alderic/w0|Why would he restrict that inheritance?|Shared knowledge makes others less dependent on the story and power he controls.|Does preserving it require secrecy?|Sometimes secrecy protected it. That was a means of survival, not its purpose forever.|Who should be able to learn it?|Those who will handle it responsibly, without a ruler claiming exclusive ownership of the past.

Alderic/w1|How do we avoid guarding it too jealously?|Teach what you understand and distinguish it from what remains uncertain.|Should every use of power be encouraged?|No. Sharing knowledge includes teaching its limits and consequences.|Will the temples still matter now?|Their inheritance extends beyond one king's reign, just as it was meant to.

King Halvard/s0|Did the others agree to your rule?|Had I waited for their agreement, I would have inherited nothing but another discussion.|You betrayed people who relied on you.|They mistook reliance for authority over me. I corrected that error.

King Halvard/s1|How safe are people who fear your guards?|Safe enough to complain about them. An indulgence they consistently fail to appreciate.|You decided what everyone else should sacrifice.|That is what a ruler does when lesser men cannot bear to choose.

King Halvard/e0|Perhaps they are afraid to object.|Then they have finally understood that interruption carries a cost.|Would you hear an honest disagreement?|A useful one, competently expressed. I have yet to hear yours.

King Halvard/e1|Fear can make people hide the truth.|A ruler learns to distinguish a useful report from a servant's excuse.|What happens when people stop being afraid?|Someone reminds them why order was preferable to their experiment.
